title: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct: Preamble and Scope
pub: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct
author: American Bar Association

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source establishes a context-sensitive framework for lawyers’ professional duties and discipline, but it does not address legal AI’s jagged capabilities, task-level gains, verification requirements, selective deployment or operating-model redesign. It therefore neither accepts nor rejects the cluster’s principal proposition.
qs: ## Scope  [14] The Rules of Professional Conduct are rules of reason.
The Rules simply provide a framework for the ethical practice of law.

st.t: Lawyer accountability: Discipline and liability remain separate
st.an: The source directly supports the cluster’s principal distinction between professional discipline and civil liability. It states that the Rules structure disciplinary regulation rather than independently create civil liability, while allowing violations to serve as evidence of breach of an otherwise applicable civil standard. It also supports limits on collateral enforcement and the distinction between authoritative Rule text and interpretive guidance.
qs: They are not designed to be a basis for civil liability.
Nevertheless, since the Rules do establish standards of conduct by lawyers, a lawyer's violation of a Rule may be evidence of breach of the applicable standard of conduct.

kp.k: Lawyers owe responsibilities beyond client representation
kp.d: The Preamble defines lawyers simultaneously as client representatives, officers of the legal system and public citizens responsible for the quality of justice. It identifies advisory, advocacy, negotiation and evaluation functions, but makes no AI-specific claim about how those functions may change.
qs: a representative of clients, an officer of the legal system and a public citizen

kp.k: Competence, diligence, communication and confidentiality are foundational
kp.d: Across professional functions, lawyers should act competently, promptly and diligently, communicate with clients and protect information relating to representations, subject to disclosures required or permitted by professional rules or other law.
qs: a lawyer should be competent, prompt and diligent
A lawyer should maintain communication with a client
A lawyer should keep in confidence information relating to representation of a client

kp.k: Lawyers should advance access to justice
kp.d: The Preamble recognises that economic and social barriers prevent both poor and some non-poor people from obtaining adequate legal assistance. It recommends that lawyers commit professional time, resources and civic influence to equal access to the justice system.
qs: the poor, and sometimes persons who are not poor, cannot afford adequate legal assistance
ensure equal access to our system of justice

kp.k: Ethical conflicts require professional and moral judgment
kp.d: The source says difficult ethical problems commonly involve tensions among duties to clients, the legal system and lawyers' own interests. Although the Rules prescribe some resolutions, professional discretion must be exercised through sensitive professional and moral judgment within the law.
qs: Virtually all difficult ethical problems arise from conflict
the exercise of sensitive professional and moral judgment

kp.k: Professional independence depends on responsible self-regulation
kp.d: The legal profession is described as largely self-governing because of its relationship with courts, government and law enforcement. Its autonomy carries a duty to regulate in the public interest rather than advance the bar's self-interested concerns, with every lawyer responsible for observing and supporting observance of the Rules.
qs: The legal profession is largely self-governing
regulations are conceived in the public interest
Every lawyer is responsible for observance of the Rules of Professional Conduct

kp.k: Rules combine obligations, permissions and role definitions
kp.d: The Scope characterises the Rules as context-sensitive rules of reason. “Shall” and “shall not” establish disciplinary requirements, “may” identifies permissible discretion, and other provisions define professional relationships and the lawyer's role.
qs: The Rules of Professional Conduct are rules of reason
Some of the Rules are imperatives
Others, generally cast in the term "may," are permissive

kp.k: Comments guide but do not create obligations
kp.d: The document distinguishes authoritative Rule text from explanatory Comments. Comments using “should” provide interpretive and compliance guidance but do not add professional obligations.
qs: Comments do not add obligations to the Rules
the text of each Rule is authoritative

kp.k: Professional rules operate within broader law
kp.d: The Rules presuppose an external legal context that includes licensing rules, statutes, court rules and substantive and procedural law. External substantive law also determines whether a client-lawyer relationship exists and therefore when many professional duties attach.
qs: The Rules presuppose a larger legal context shaping the lawyer's role
principles of substantive law external to these Rules determine

kp.k: Compliance rests primarily on understanding and voluntariness
kp.d: The Scope presents enforcement as only one component of compliance: understanding and voluntary compliance come first, followed by peer and public opinion and, when necessary, disciplinary proceedings. It also states that the Rules do not exhaust lawyers' moral and ethical considerations.
qs: depends primarily upon understanding and voluntary compliance
The Rules simply provide a framework for the ethical practice of law

kp.d: A Rule violation can invoke discipline, but assessment must reflect the circumstances and information available when the lawyer acted. Sanctions depend on factors including willfulness, seriousness, extenuating circumstances and prior violations.
qs: made on the basis of the facts and circumstances
depend on all the circumstances

kp.k: Rule violations do not automatically create civil liability
kp.d: The Scope says a violation should not itself create a cause of action, a presumption of breached legal duty or an automatic nondisciplinary remedy. Nevertheless, a violation may serve as evidence concerning the applicable standard of conduct.
qs: They are not designed to be a basis for civil liability
may be evidence of breach of the applicable standard of conduct

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: No AI-related claims or predictions are present.
pts.d: The ABA Preamble and Scope describe lawyers' professional responsibilities and the interpretation and application of the Model Rules. They do not mention AI or claim that AI changes legal services, professional roles, or legal markets. Applying these general principles to AI would be an inference beyond the supplied source.
